entities.name: NBC Sports
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
NBC Sports is the sports division of NBCUniversal, one of the United States' most historically significant sports broadcasting entities — with a legacy dating to NBC's earliest television sports programming (1940s-1950s) and encompassing decades of Olympics coverage, NFL football, NBA basketball, Notre Dame football, Premier League soccer, and numerous other major sports properties, establishing NBC as one of the two or three most important networks in American sports television history.

NBC's Olympics broadcasting legacy is particularly remarkable: NBC has broadcast more Olympic Games than any other American network, beginning with the 1964 Tokyo Summer Olympics and continuing through the 2032 deals that extend NBC's Olympic broadcasting rights for decades. The Olympics have been simultaneously NBC's most prestigious and most financially risky programming: the network has lost money on some Olympics while profiting significantly from others, with the rights costs escalating dramatically.

NBC Sports' portfolio has evolved dramatically with the digital transformation: the launch of NBC Sports Network (originally Versus, then NBC Sports Network, then merged into USA Network in 2022) and the Peacock streaming service's acquisition of various sports rights represent the continuing evolution from traditional broadcast to multi-platform sports media. The acquisition of Premier League rights (2013) was transformative for American soccer audiences, dramatically expanding Premier League viewership in the United States from its previously minimal American presence.
